markdown_report:
The strongest early direction is **inference-aligned terminal-mask training**, supported by diagnostics that verify BERT4Rec semantics before interpreting ranking weaknesses. No experiment results are available; all proposed benefits remain hypotheses.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Sampled positive–negative margins measure local separation. They cannot establish improvement in the pinned HR@10 evaluation. (2) Bidirectional attention makes target visibility a critical correctness issue. Diagnostics must distinguish masked targets from visible items. (3) User feedback suggests broad relevance sometimes displaces specific recent matches. It does not establish ownership, compatibility, mood, or present intent.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) uses masked-item learning and includes last-item masking. This supports testing training examples that match appended-mask inference. (2) [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show that sampled metrics can misrepresent ranking comparisons. Training margins therefore remain diagnostic, while the fixed host evaluator determines selection. (3) [TemProxRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784) examines temporal information beyond order. Recent-versus-old history perturbations are consequently useful sensitivity probes, but cannot establish current intent.

**Framework and directions.** Organize evidence into three layers: semantic correctness → training/inference alignment → behavioral sensitivity. The corresponding checks are target-visibility and readout audits, terminal-mask supervision, and matched recent/older deletions. Benchmark HR@10 remains the shared outcome; diagnostic measures explain possible mechanisms.

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores use originality/potential/implementation difficulty, each from 0–10; higher difficulty means harder.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Target-visibility audit [BERT4Rec] | 3/7/3 | Essential correctness evidence; inexpensive and reusable | Primarily verification; limited direct ranking benefit; tracing requires sampler access |
| Terminal-mask sampling [BERT4Rec] | 3/8/4 | Direct inference alignment; feasible controlled ablation | Established technique; benefit depends on baseline sampling; writer consistency requires care |
| Recent/older deletion probe [TemProxRec] | 4/6/4 | Tests temporal sensitivity with available histories | Descriptive evidence; uncertain downstream benefit; matched deletions need care |

**Selected algorithm.** Introduce one sampling probability, α, controlling examples with only a terminal masked target. Retain the corrected baseline’s random-mask objective for remaining examples. If the baseline already implements this mixture, vary only α; do not present existing behavior as a new contribution.

```text
sample a training-only history prefix and its terminal item
with probability α:
    input = left_pad(truncate(prefix + [MASK]))
    supervise terminal MASK with the removed terminal item
otherwise:
    use baseline masked-item corruption and supervision
optimize the baseline loss on supervised positions
```

Audit target removal, padding attention, and final-nonpadding readout. Compare baseline α against one prespecified alternative using seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches/epoch. Train one model/category; select using four-category macro validation HR@10. Preserve routing, DATA_DIR, ModelView, diagnostic entry points, and predictor-writer/checkpoint consistency. Report empty probes as unavailable, never healthy zeros.

idea.description: Test a single change to BERT4Rec: the probability of terminal-mask-only training examples, matching appended-mask next-item inference while retaining baseline random masked-item learning.
idea.motivation: The diagnosis suggests insufficient distinction between broad relevance and a compelling next choice. Terminal-mask supervision provides a feasible objective-alignment hypothesis without inventing user attributes or changing the model family. Improvement must be established by the pinned validation evaluator.
idea.implementation_notes: First inspect the supplied baseline during host implementation to determine its existing terminal-mask probability. Change only that probability for the initial ablation. Use training histories exclusively; remove the supervised terminal item before constructing its masked input. Preserve the reserved mask token, baseline positional conventions and truncation, padding-key masking, and final-nonpadding readout. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum epochs 200, and batches per epoch 200. Train exactly one independent BERT4Rec model per category, with no score fusion or checkpoint averaging. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; artifacts stay under the trial directory. Synchronize architecture and configuration in the predictor writer and working/predict.py. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all ModelView interfaces. Compute diagnostic margins only at valid masked supervised positions; return counts and explicit unavailable values for empty probes. No unavailable review or product attributes are used.
idea.pseudocode:
For each baseline training batch:
  Sample training-only history prefixes using the existing sampler.
  For each example, draw terminal_only ~ Bernoulli(alpha).
  If terminal_only:
    Separate prefix into context and terminal target.
    Construct left-padded, truncated context followed by reserved MASK.
    Place the target label only at that MASK position.
  Else:
    Apply the corrected baseline masked-item sampler.
  Compute baseline loss only at supervised positions and update one model.
Before evaluation:
  Verify terminal targets were removed before mask insertion.
  Verify readout indexes max(where(sequence != 0)).
  Verify embedded predictor reproduces training-side evaluation scores.
Evaluate with the unchanged host validation protocol and compare macro HR@10.

originality.positive: Combines inference alignment with explicit family-specific semantic verification in this constrained diagnostic workflow.
originality.negative: Last-item masking is already part of published BERT4Rec; tuning its frequency is an incremental contribution.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result can clarify whether objective alignment warrants further work on next-item supervision.
future_potential.negative: The baseline may already be well aligned, and increased terminal supervision may reduce useful contextual learning.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires a small sampler change and retains the existing backbone and scoring architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct truncation, target removal, diagnostic masking, and predictor consistency require careful verification.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item modeling for sequential recommendation.
Uses an appended mask for next-item prediction and includes last-item masking during training.
limitations: Does not establish the best terminal-mask sampling probability for these four benchmark datasets.
Bidirectional training requires careful corruption to prevent supervised-target visibility.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can yield inconsistent model comparisons.
Supports separating sampled-margin diagnostics from benchmark selection.
limitations: Does not provide evidence that the proposed training change improves this benchmark.
Does not replace the task's mandatory pinned evaluator.

related_work.title: TemProxRec
contributions: Studies temporal information beyond sequence order.
Motivates examining recent and older interaction evidence separately.
limitations: Temporal sensitivity does not establish user mood, ownership, or immediate need.
Provides motivation for a diagnostic probe, not validation of terminal-mask sampling.
